request.question: How much of the rise is in our control?

answer:
**C1 cash cost climbed +1.18 USD/t last quarter, and roughly 1.27 USD/t (>100%) of that increase came from operational levers under site control—diesel efficiency (+0.24 USD/t), tyre wear (+0.12 USD/t), and especially maintenance (+0.67 USD/t)—while lower volumes added +0.27 USD/t and favourable price movements (-0.04 USD/t) provided minor relief.**

### Cost bridge Q4 FY2026 → Q1 FY2027 (USD/t)

| Lever               | Impact | Provenance | In our control? |
|---------------------|--------|------------|-----------------|
| **Start (Q4 FY2026)** | 20.16  | MIXED (Cost: stand-in · Drivers: FMS, historian) | – |
| Volume              | +0.27  | MIXED (stand-in cost postings) | Partially |
| Diesel Efficiency   | +0.24  | MIXED (Litres per tonne: FMS haul cycles) | **Yes** |
| Tyre Wear           | +0.12  | MIXED (stand-in cost postings) | **Yes** |
| Maintenance         | +0.67  | MIXED (stand-in cost postings) | **Yes** |
| Price               | −0.04  | MIXED (stand-in cost postings) | No |
| Other               | −0.09  | MIXED (stand-in cost postings) | Partially |
| **End (Q1 FY2027)**   | 21.33  | MIXED (Cost: stand-in · Drivers: FMS, historian) | – |

**Chain:** The 0.67 USD/t maintenance spike (Q1 FY2027 maintenance-order cost jumped to 0.94 USD/t from 0.27 USD/t in Q4 FY2026; fleet maintenance rose to 2.10 from 2.07 USD/t—MIXED provenance, stand-in cost postings) signals unplanned work or parts shortfall, while diesel efficiency deteriorated (queue time or haul distance per FMS cycles).

**Next step:** Investigate the Q1 maintenance-order spike with a Pareto of work orders by equipment class and failure mode to target the top driver for the next two weeks.
